intro: A Cajun fiddler and singer from Louisiana.
story: Courtney Granger was a fiddler and singer from Lafayette, Louisiana, of the Balfa family lineage, who started singing in bars around age 13. He played and toured full time for years with the Pine Leaf Boys and Balfa Toujours. His solo country debut, Beneath Still Waters, was produced by Dirk Powell and released on Valcour Records. He came to Pickathon in 2017 and sat for an interview there about his Cajun and Creole roots and songwriting. He died in 2021.
artist_reel_line: He died in 2021, remembered as one of the great voices of his generation.

intro: A roots-reggae singer from St. Croix.
story: Dezarie is a roots reggae singer from St. Croix, in the U.S. Virgin Islands, who works closely with the band Midnite, who played on her records. She was named Best New Female Reggae Artist in Atlanta in 2001, the year of Fya, then returned to St. Croix. Gracious Mama Africa came in 2003, Eaze the Pain in 2008, The Fourth Book in 2010 and Live in Your Meditation in November 2014. She played Pickathon in 2017, released Guardian in 2025, and in August 2026 had a main-stage set at Reggae on the River.

intro: Elder statesmen of loud, fuzzed guitar.
story: Dinosaur Jr. is the Amherst, Massachusetts band of J Mascis, Lou Barlow and Murph, whose original trio reunited in 2005. Give a Glimpse of What Yer Not came out on Jagjaguwar on August 5, 2016, produced by Mascis at his Bisquiteen studio in Amherst, the reunion's fourth album and their 11th overall; the A.V. Club gave it an A-, and Stereogum made it Album of the Week. They played Pickathon in 2017. Sweep It Into Space followed in 2021, and There Near, on Jagjaguwar, in August 2026.

intro: A Virginia singer with a plain mountain-country voice.
story: Dori Freeman is a singer-songwriter from Galax, Virginia, a hub of traditional music, who grew up in a musical family; her grandfather Willard Gayheart wrote one of the songs on her second album. Her self-titled debut came out on Free Dirt in 2016, and Letters Never Read on Blue Hens Music on October 20, 2017, both produced by Teddy Thompson, the second with Richard Thompson, Aoife O'Donovan and Kacy & Clayton. She played Pickathon that year. Every Single Star followed in 2019, Ten Thousand Roses in 2021, and in 2026 she announced a sixteen-song retrospective of ten years.

intro: Melina Duterte's home-recorded pop, just breaking out.
story: Melina Duterte was born on March 25, 1994, in Walnut Creek, California, and Jay Som began as her bedroom recording project in the Bay Area. Everybody Works came out on Polyvinyl and Double Denim on March 10, 2017, and Pitchfork ranked it No. 26 among the year's best albums; it also landed on 2017 best-of lists at NPR, Stereogum, Rolling Stone and Billboard. She played Pickathon that summer. Anak Ko came in 2019, and after years working with others, boygenius among them, Belong, her fourth album, came out on Polyvinyl in October 2025.

intro: An Australian songwriter of quiet heartbreak.
story: Julia Jacklin was born on August 30, 1990, in the Blue Mountains of Australia, and quit a job at an essential-oil factory to focus on music. Her debut, Don't Let the Kids Win, came out on October 7, 2016, produced by Ben Edwards, and The Guardian's Michael Hann called it an impressive indie-country debut that will slowly creep into many people's affections. She played Pickathon in 2017 and again in 2019, the year of Crushing, and Pre Pleasure followed in 2022. The Gem, on 4AD, came out in September 2026.

intro: A North Carolina duo, here for the third of five visits.
story: Blindfaller, their fifth album, came out on Yep Roc in 2016, after Such Jubilee. Andrew Marlin and Emily Frantz played Pickathon in 2014 and 2015 and came back in 2017. Tides of a Teardrop followed on February 1, 2019, reaching No. 164 on the Billboard 200 and No. 2 on the Folk chart. They returned to the farm in 2019 and 2023, renamed themselves Watchhouse in 2021, and released Rituals on Thirty Tigers in 2025.

intro: A Seattle Hammond organ trio with a sax partner.
story: McTuff is the Seattle organ trio of the Hammond B3 player Joe Doria, formed in 2008 as a tribute to the organists Jimmy Smith and Jack McDuff, with the guitarist Andy Coe, the drummer D'Vonne Lewis and often the saxophonist Skerik. OG McTuff Vol. 1 came out in 2009 and Vol. 2: After the Show in 2011, and they held a residency at Seattle's Seamonster Lounge for over five years. They played Pickathon in 2017 billed as McTuff feat. Skerik. KNKX recorded a studio session in February 2026 and said they have given the Northwest two decades of grooves, and in August they reunited with Crack Sabbath at Nectar Lounge.

intro: A Seattle saxophonist, here with McTuff.
story: Skerik is the Seattle saxophonist Eric Walton, born on November 19, 1964, a founding member of Critters Buggin, Garage a Trois and Tuatara. He has played with Les Claypool's Frog Brigade and Fancy Band, with Mad Season, and with R.E.M.'s Peter Buck in Tuatara. He came to Pickathon in 2017 in a joint set with the organ trio McTuff. Garage a Trois released Calm Down Cologne in 2021, he was resident artist of the 2024 Earshot Jazz Festival, and in August 2026 he joined a Crack Sabbath reunion at Nectar Lounge.

intro: A Southern indie-rock band from Charleston.
story: Susto is the Charleston, South Carolina band fronted by Justin Osborne, who said the name comes from his songwriting style, an attempt to express an ongoing state of susto. Their first self-titled album came in 2014, and & I'm Fine Today on January 13, 2017, took over two years, with friends and College of Charleston students adding instruments. They played Pickathon that year. Ever Since I Lost My Mind came out on Rounder, My Entire Life on New West in 2023, and in late 2026 Osborne began a Charleston residency of full-album sets.

intro: A high-voltage pop-rock band from Austin.
story: Sweet Spirit is the Austin band fronted by Sabrina Ellis, put together around 2014 after her earlier band Bobby Jealousy broke up; Ellis also leads A Giant Dog. Cokomo, their first album, came out on Nine Mile in 2015, and a second full-length followed in spring 2017, the year they played Pickathon. Trinidad came out on Merge in 2020, and Andrew Cashen planned a songwriting event in Austin in November 2026.

intro: A Portland rapper respected in the underground.
story: Alana Chenevert was born on May 26, 1987, in Los Angeles and moved to Portland in 2013; the name is a nod to her hometown and a habit of dodging trouble. Bone Music, made with the Portland producer Neill Von Tally, came out on EYRST on February 3, 2017, and Pitchfork gave it a 7.2, by the Portland Mercury's account. She played Pickathon that year. She sang backup with Blossom for Aminé's Tonight Show performance of "Caroline" in November 2016, and her major-label album came out on Unsociable/Interscope on August 19, 2022. In 2025 she returned with the EP databreach001: Mr. I Don't Miss.
artist_reel_line: Her 2025 EP databreach001: Mr. I Don't Miss followed work with Anderson .Paak.

intro: A garage-rock dynamo, back for a fourth visit.
story: Ty Segall is a Bay Area garage-rock prodigy who relocated from San Francisco to Los Angeles around 2014, known for an album a year plus side projects. Manipulator, his seventh solo album, came out on Drag City on August 26, 2014 after a 14-month writing process, and he played nearly every instrument; NPR called it the rock record of the summer. He played Pickathon in 2013, 2015, 2016 and 2017. Freedom's Goblin followed in 2018, Possession, billed as his 17th album, in May 2025, and Chrome in 2026, with the EP Love Fuzzz.
